facts.fact: The World Bank's concept-stage document states that Chad's civil registration system is essentially paper based with no consolidated database, decentralised and managed by local governments under the supervision of the Ministry of Territorial Administration and Decentralization; undated, so the document's date is used.

The civil registration system is managed by local governments under the supervision of the Ministry of Territorial Administration and Decentralization, and the digitalisation of civil registration services and creation of a centralised civil registry under the state agency ANATS is described as under way; undated, so the document's date is used.

The document states that the Government of Chad, drawing on APAI-CRVS guidelines, developed a strategic plan to systematically strengthen civil registration; the plan's title, dates and cost are not given, and the document's date is used.

The proposed US$120 million IDA-financed Chad Digital Transformation Project includes sub-component 3.2 to digitalise the civil registration system, within a component 3 indicatively costed at US$42 million, at concept stage on 27 February 2023; no domestic budget line is stated.

systems.owner: local governments, under the supervision of the Ministère de l'Administration du Territoire et de la Décentralisation (MATD)
systems.tiers: decentralised, local governments; 26 per cent of new births registered

systems.system: Centralised civil registry under ANATS (under way)
systems.tiers: national, being created; with integration with health and veterinary services to reach nomadic groups

systems.system: SIGPTS, with its National Biometric Register of Populations (RNBP) module
systems.tiers: national; introduced in 2020; issues the national identification number, national ID card, passport and immigration documents; 3 per cent of the population over 12 holds a national ID card

note: The document says Chad manages civil registration and the national ID card as two separate systems. The centralised registry under ANATS is described as under way, with nothing on which offices use it; the project's results indicator is to be the number of new births registered 'digitally enabled'.
